title: Remembering notable Hollywood figures in 2026
body_md:
A late-November retrospective on notable entertainment industry deaths in 2026 offers an occasion to revisit the careers of artists whose work reached several generations of audiences. This draft draws on a report dated November 26, 2026. The death notices discussed here are attributed to that report and have not been independently verified for this draft.

Among the film performers included is Robert Duvall, whose credits encompass The Godfather, Apocalypse Now and The Apostle. His career illustrates how understated acting can give complex characters a lasting presence on screen. The report lists his age at death as 95. Catherine O'Hara, another featured performer, built a distinctive comic career across projects including Home Alone and Schitt's Creek. Her ability to combine exaggerated comic behavior with recognizable human vulnerability helped make those performances memorable.

The retrospective also names Sam Neill, whose work ranges from Jurassic Park to The Piano, and Patrick Stewart, whose stage experience informed his performances in Star Trek and the X-Men films. Their careers demonstrate the range of dramatic approaches that can coexist within popular genre entertainment. Tim Curry, associated with The Rocky Horror Picture Show and the television adaptation of It, is another performer included in the report, with a body of work that often embraced unconventional and theatrical characters.

Television is represented by James Van Der Beek, remembered for Dawson's Creek, and Eric Dane, whose role as Mark Sloan became a prominent part of Grey's Anatomy. The report also includes R.J. Mitte, known for playing Walter White Jr. in Breaking Bad. These performers are associated with different eras of television drama, illustrating how serialized storytelling has changed while continuing to create enduring connections with viewers.

The entertainment business extends well beyond actors appearing on camera. Peter Cullen, the voice closely associated with Optimus Prime in Transformers, exemplifies the importance of voice performance to the identity of a fictional character. Media executive Ted Turner, also named in the retrospective, helped reshape television distribution through CNN and other cable networks.

The report additionally covers figures from music, costume design and other creative fields. Their inclusion provides a reminder that popular culture depends on a wide network of artists, technicians and institutions rather than screen performers alone.

This selection is not a comprehensive account of the year's losses, and 2026 has not yet concluded. Revisiting the work of the artists named can help audiences appreciate the history behind contemporary entertainment. Before public publication, however, the individual death reports should be checked against reliable independent reporting and official announcements.
